You are on the support-desk Genkit app in this directory. Bug report: The replies that draftReply writes for customer tickets stop after the first line, usually just "Dear customer," or "Hi there,". There is no error, and the reason it reports for stopping looks normal. I expected a complete reply that explains the next steps and signs off from the support team.
Find the root cause and fix it in the app's source. Then write `answer.json` in the project root: { "file": "<path of the file that had the bug>", "snippet": "<the exact broken text you replaced, copied verbatim, one line is enough>", "cause": "<one sentence>", "evidence": "<what shows this is the cause>" }. Don't change `package.json` or add dependencies.
I should start by exploring /reeval/workspace, since the user mentioned the support-desk Genkit app is located there.
I'll start by finding the draftReply source in the support-desk app.

text: Found it—draftReply has a stopSequences config set to stop at the first newline, which cuts off generation early. The fix is to remove that stopSequences setting. Let me also peek at ai.ts and agents.ts to confirm there's nothing else causing truncation, like a maxOutputTokens limit.
The `draftReply` flow passes `config: { stopSequences: ['\n'] }`, which would cut generation at the first newline. Before editing, I'll check `ai.ts` for any other config that could contribute.

input.command: cd .; cat src/ai.ts; echo ---; grep -rn "stopSequences\|maxOutputTokens" src prompts; echo ---; cat .gitignore
input.description: Check ai.ts and search for other stop/token config

text: Found the root cause: the stopSequences array with a newline character in draftReply is cutting things short. I'll remove that line and update answer.json. I can't fully verify without an API key, but I could at least typecheck with tsc --noEmit after making the edit.
The only stop-sequence config is the `['\n']` on line 64 of `src/flows.ts`, so that's the root cause. I'll remove it.
Now I'll write `answer.json` and typecheck the project without changing dependencies.

text: Type checking passes, but I likely can't run the live model without an API key, so I'll note in the report that I wasn't able to verify actual runtime behavior, keeping the summary brief.

The root cause was a stop sequence on the newline in `draftReply`. I removed it from `src/flows.ts` (the `config: { stopSequences: ['\n'] },` line), so the model no longer halts at the first line break. I wrote `answer.json` in the project root and it parses; `tsc --noEmit` passes.

I did not run `draftReply` against the live model, since that needs a Gemini API key. The fix is confirmed by reading the code, not by a reply from the model. `package.json` is unchanged.
